claims.text: Setting an environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service allows Terraform and OpenTofu to use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud instance as a state backend.
The Pulumi state-backend integration for Terraform is documented at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/.
The `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable sets the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service.
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves the `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` domain.

Using a separate domain for the Terraform-compatible API (distinct from `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`) is not required; `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` can be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` to avoid a second DNS record.

In Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, the value of `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` should be used wherever the state backend guide (/docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/) uses `tf.pulumi.com`.
The Pulumi state backend guide for Terraform uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the example domain.
